routes.summary: The analysis of the system over the daily aggregates: times, waits, cost, coverage, bottlenecks, and a comparison between two periods or two scenarios
Swap the API token: the old one stops working at once; the new one is in api-token
Cancels an Actor in flight; the Director judges; idempotent by Idempotency-Key
Pauses an Actor in flight, saving its checkpoint; idempotent by Idempotency-Key
Resumes a paused Actor by the policy of the cause; idempotent by Idempotency-Key
The spending caps (per profile and per Executor) with what each has spent
One-use ticket to open the chat socket of a scenario (valid for 30 s)
The / commands valid for a scenario now, by its type and state, the commands of the client of the Director included
The effective configuration, with every value that could be a secret held back
Edits keys of the configuration file with the validation of a start; ui, chat, limits and roles apply at once, the rest on restart
Stop the daemon: it answers first, then shuts down as on a signal
Answers a pending decision of the Producer; idempotent by Idempotency-Key
One direct session with its conversation
Stops the turn that runs in a direct session; `cancelled: false` when none runs
Closes a direct session: the client ends, the worktree is committed and removed and the branch stays or goes by `direct_session.on_close`
Runs a command of the client in a direct session (`chat.client_commands` and `chat.slash_access` apply); 403 when not allowed; idempotent by Idempotency-Key
Writes to the Actor of a direct session and starts a turn; 409 while a turn runs; idempotent by Idempotency-Key
Sends the result of a direct session to a demand (an idea of the queue) or a piece (a play); idempotent by Idempotency-Key
The events a direct session trajectory is built from (messages, tools, permissions, closing), oldest first, by cursor
Event stream with resume by Last-Event-ID: history after the cursor, then live
Executors of the configuration and of the table, by id, by cursor
Health of the daemon: 200 once the reconciliation of the start-up ended without error; 503 before that or while stopping
Ideas in the order they arrived, by cursor; filter by state, scenario, play and group
One idea
Sets an idea aside for later, with the reason
Drops an idea for good, with the reason
Puts a deferred idea back in the queue
Layout preferences of an interface (the default when none was saved)
Replaces the layout preferences of an interface
Orders (in force, scheduled, ended) in the order they were given, by cursor
Gives an order (an instruction, a rule or a suspension); idempotent by Idempotency-Key
One order
Changes the validity of an order (`for` counts from the current end)
Revokes an order, with the reason
Suspends a global order in one scenario by giving a local suspension order
One play with its stages and demands
The play as an ATIF v1.8 trajectory (the Director as the root, each attempt embedded); with attemptId, that attempt alone
Attempts of a play, oldest first, by cursor, with Actor, state and pause; filter by open
The latest version of each key of the blackboard of a play, by key, by cursor
One key of the blackboard of a play: the latest version, or the one asked for
The versions of one key of the blackboard of a play, oldest first, by cursor
Cancels a play that is not finished; idempotent by Idempotency-Key
The diff of the latest attempt of a demand against the branch of its play
Pauses a play: nothing new opens until it resumes; idempotent by Idempotency-Key
Resumes a paused play; idempotent by Idempotency-Key
The spans the daemon made for a play (stages, attempts, sessions, tool calls, waits) as a tree with the durations
The events a play trajectory is built from (sessions, turns, tools, permissions, attempts), oldest first, by cursor
The installed plugins, with the state of each one in each project
One plugin: the manifest and the text of what it asks for before it is turned on

__schema2.description: The version of this format; the only one is 1.

__schema3.description: Plugin id; the events are plugin.<id>.<name>.

command.description: The command as an argument list, run with no shell: ["node", "dist/server.js"].

args.description: More arguments, appended to the command.

cwd.description: Working directory, relative to the folder of the plugin (the default).

url.description: The Streamable HTTP endpoint of the server, in the loopback only.

roles.description: The roles that see the tool; empty when only the panel uses it.

effects.description: What the tool changes: read, local_write, network or external_write.

requires_producer_approval.description: When true, every call waits for the approval of the Producer.

__schema16.description: Names read from the vault and handed only to the server of the plugin.

__schema19.description: Event names, with no prefix: the daemon publishes them as plugin.<id>.<name>.

tool.description: A tool of this plugin; the call follows its requires_producer_approval.

__schema25.description: A tool of this plugin with effects: read; its result fills the block.

__schema27.description: One catalog per language; "en" is required, and what a language lacks shows in "en".

__schema28.description: Screen texts by key, with "{{name}}" placeholders where the text has variables.

routes.summary: Runs an action of the panel for the Producer; it asks the Producer first when the tool needs it
Turns a plugin off in a project
Turns a plugin on in a project, approving the manifest that was shown
The panel of a plugin in a project: the blocks with their data and texts
Accounts with the state of the quota of each, in the order they were made, by cursor
Registers an account (a subscription profile or an API key profile); idempotent
Drains and removes an account: its directory, its secret and its Executors
One account with its quota state
Stops giving new sessions to an account and waits for the running ones
Opens the official login of a subscription account and answers its mode, URL and code
Cancels the open login of an account and ends the process of the login
Hands the open login of an account the code the browser shows
The ordered Executor list of each role, with the next Executor and the exhaustion rule
Scenarios (projects, tasks, chats), oldest first, by cursor; filter by kind and state
Opens a scenario (a project or a chat) and its Director; idempotent by Idempotency-Key
WebSocket of the chat with the Director; authenticated by a ticket, not by the token
One scenario with its repositories, overrides and counts of open plays and decisions
Attachments of a scenario (metadata only), in the order they came, by cursor
Attaches a file of the daemon machine or a pasted text to a scenario; idempotent
Metadata of one attachment
The content of one attachment: text, or base64 for an image or a binary file

Judgment points of a scenario, oldest first, by cursor; filter by state, play and kind

Runs one pass of the idea queue of a scenario now (`/idea drain`)
Plays of a scenario, oldest first, by cursor; filter by open and state
The setup assistant: whether a first run is needed, and the run to resume in each flow
Starts a run of a setup flow (a run in progress of the flow is a conflict: resume it)
Goes back one step, undoing only the state of the step it leaves
Cancels a run; nothing was written to the configuration
Confirms the review: writes the whole result to the configuration at once
Answers the current step of a run; the daemon validates it and moves to the next

Looks for the clients again without a restart (on Windows also in the Path of the registry); a client found enters the pool
State of the daemon: pid, version, data folder, state, daemon id and API version
The state of the telemetry: the OTLP receiver and its refused batches, the base, and the export with its drops
What the daemon knows about new versions: the mode, the version found and whether it is ready

Applies the version that is ready, at the moment `updates.apply_when` says (or `park` or `wait` as the answer to the question of the max_wait); 409 `conflict` when there is none, the mode is `off` or `check`, or this is not the own executable
Searches for a new version now (the mode `off` answers 409 `conflict`); returns the status after the search
Consumption totals, optionally split by session, play, profile or Executor
